notes:
Full RSS capture, 34 processes with nonzero VmRSS (captured via /proc/<pid>/status on the live device; the capture script's own process is excluded from this list). System-level used memory (MemTotal - MemAvailable, per Section 3.5 MEM-006 guidance) is 582.0 MiB — up sharply from the 172-176 MiB range in earlier snapshots. totalRssMB (524.08) is the GROSS sum of listed processes and double-counts shared pages; it does not equal the 582.0 MiB system-level figure. 

This capture surfaces a severe growth finding: onewifi_em_agent, previously measured at 20.24 MiB (the earlier full-process capture), is now 363.7 MiB — an approximately 18x increase, and by far the dominant contributor to the profile's memory use (exceeding OneWifi's own 54.0 MiB by nearly 7x). No prior capture exists between these two data points, so the growth curve shape (steady vs. sudden) is unknown; unlike the gateway's three-point onewifi_em_ctrl/onewifi_em_agent history, this is only a two-point comparison, but the magnitude here is substantially larger than the gateway's own onewifi_em_agent growth. This is the single strongest signal yet toward a genuine memory leak in the EasyMesh agent component (present on both profiles) rather than legitimate mesh-state growth, and materially increases the priority of running the formal 72-hour soak test (MEM-008 criterion) before this profile's RAM floor can be considered validated. Extender-specific note: this profile runs onewifi_em_agent only (no onewifi_em_ctrl, which is gateway/controller-only), so this single process is the entire EasyMesh agent footprint for this device.
